entry.title: Gemini LaTeX in Google Docs™: When an Equation Stays as Text, and the Fix

link.title: Gemini LaTeX in Google Docs™: When an Equation Stays as Text, and the Fix

entry.summary: Most of the time, Gemini’s maths arrives in Google Docs™ as equations already. Copy the answer and paste it, or send it with Gemini’s Export to Docs, and inline and single-line formulas come in as Docs equations, with nothing for you to do. entry.title: How to Write an Equation in LaTeX: The Five Basics

link.title: How to Write an Equation in LaTeX: The Five Basics

entry.summary: To write an equation in LaTeX, put the maths between delimiters — $…$ inside a sentence, \[ … \] on its own line — and write it with a few building blocks: ^ and _ for superscripts and subscripts, \frac{}{} and \sqrt{} for fractions and roots, backslash names such as \alpha for symbols, and \sum or \int with limits. Those five pieces cover most of the equations in a typical course or paper. ...

link.title: LaTeX vs Word for a Thesis: Draft in One, Submit in Other
